## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Verdict | Confidence | Severity | Task Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Confirmed | High | Medium | Correctness / focused regression |

### What Was Claimed

The required verification preflight can accept `npm tst` without validating that the selected package defines a usable `test` script. The finding was reported against `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` and requests a narrowly scoped fix plus regression coverage.

### What We Found

The current preflight identifies package-manager commands in `packageScriptName`. It recognizes only `command === "test"` (lines 130–133), while npm exposes `t`, `tst`, and `test` as aliases for the test lifecycle. For `npm tst`, the function returns `undefined`, so `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` skips `assertPackageScript`; a malformed or missing root `scripts.test` entry can therefore pass preflight as long as the executable exists. The existing focused tests cover `npm test` and rejected package-selector options but do not cover `npm tst` or `npm t`.

### Root Cause

Test-script validation is keyed to one spelling of the npm lifecycle command instead of the complete supported npm alias set. The executable availability check remains correct; the missing alias-to-`test` mapping is the bypass.

### Affected Files

| Path | Area | Change Needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | package-manager command parsing | Map `test`, `t`, and `tst` to the `test` package script while retaining option rejection. |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | preflight regression coverage | Assert aliases reject malformed root test metadata and accept a package cwd with a valid test script. |

### Evidence

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:130–133` handles only `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` command spelling `test`.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts:57–60` calls `assertPackageScript` only when `packageScriptName` returns a script.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts:87–120` tests malformed metadata and selector rejection but has no `t`/`tst` alias case.
- The fixture's root malformed `scripts.test` value is an object, while its `web` package has a valid string test script, making both bypass and intended validation outcomes directly testable.

### History Findings

The issue cites prior review finding VP-003 from PR #110 and states that an earlier remediation recognized aliases. The frozen integration base still contains the single-spelling implementation and lacks alias regression coverage, so the finding remains reproducible on this run. No history-based scope expansion is warranted.

### Recommendation

Add a small alias set check (`test`, `t`, `tst`) that returns the canonical script name `test`; retain `assertNoPackageManagerOptions` for all aliases. Extend the focused test to exercise `npm tst` (and the equivalent `npm t`) against malformed root metadata and a valid package cwd. Do not change command execution, policy schema, or unrelated package-manager behavior.

### Related Issues

- Source issue: #94.
- Source pull request: #110, finding VP-003.
- Current remediation issue: #113.

### Decomposition Assessment

Single bounded implementation. Two files, one parser branch, and focused regression coverage; no decomposition or product decision required.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] `npm test`, `npm t`, and `npm tst` all validate the canonical `test` script in the selected package.
- [ ] A missing or non-string `scripts.test` is rejected for each alias before execution.
- [ ] A package cwd with a valid string `scripts.test` is accepted for each alias.
- [ ] Existing option and executable preflight behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->
